interface.name: list_order_statuses
interface.title: List Order Statuses
interface.description: Returns every order state this store uses -- id, slug, display name, parent and whether it is active -- so any flow that filters, reports on or moves orders by state uses a state the store actually has.
whenToUse: A merchant names an order state in words -- 'returned', 'still under review', 'the ones out for delivery' -- and another tool needs that state's id. Resolve the wording here first: a store renames the built-in states and adds its own, so the merchant's words never map reliably to a fixed list.
Before reading orders narrowed to a state with list_orders.

Before anything that TARGETS orders in a state rather than merely reading them -- a coupon for customers whose orders are stuck mid-fulfilment, a report on one stage of delivery -- the state must be resolved before that tool is called.
The merchant asks which states their orders can be in, or which custom states they have added on top of the built-in ones.
A status-filtered call came back with no orders and there is no other reason to expect none -- the state may not exist under the name that was guessed, or the wrong id was passed.
whenNotToUse: The merchant wants the orders themselves rather than the list of states -- resolve the state here, then call list_orders with it.
The merchant wants to move one order into a different state -- resolve the target state here, then use update_order_status; this tool only reads.
The state is already known from earlier in the same conversation -- a store's states change rarely, so do not re-fetch this per order or once per flow.

id.description: THIS store's own id for the state. It is the id sibling order tools take; it is not stable across stores, which is why it has to be looked up rather than remembered.

name.description: The state as the merchant sees it, in the store's own language -- usually Arabic. Quote this one back to a merchant.

slug.description: The canonical Salla family the state belongs to, e.g. 'under_review' or 'restored'. NOT unique: a parent state and every custom state the merchant added under it share one slug, so a slug alone does not identify a state.

type.description: 'original' for a state Salla supplies, 'custom' for one the merchant added.

is_active.description: Whether the state is in use. Do not offer an inactive state to a merchant or filter on one.

sort.description: The state's position among its siblings, following the store's own fulfilment order.

original.description: The canonical Salla state this one derives from -- {id, name}. Where a store's own id is not what an endpoint wants, this is the id that is the same across every store.

parent.description: The state this one sits under -- {id, name} -- or null for a top-level state. States are two levels deep: a merchant's custom state hangs off the built-in one it refines, e.g. 'partially returned' under 'returned'.

translations.description: The state's name and customer message per language code, e.g. {'en': {'name': 'Delivered'}, 'ar': {...}}. Match an English word from the merchant against this when `name` is in another language.

components._comment: type separates Salla's own statuses from the merchant's custom ones.

http.summary: List Order Statuses -- list all order statuses the store uses, including the custom ones the merchant has added.

statuses.meaning: The store's access token is missing, expired, or does not carry the orders.read scope, so the store's order states cannot be read until the app's authorization is fixed.
